daily_brief: Europe faces an acute climate-energy nexus crisis as Romania fully shut down its only nuclear power plant due to record-low Danube water levels, removing 20% of the country's electricity capacity and forcing reliance on imports [BBC, RFI, Le Monde]. This development coincides with France evacuating hundreds as wildfires spread through the Landes region amid an unprecedented fire season [France 24]. Meanwhile, US-China trade tensions escalated sharply as the White House accused over 40 countries—including India, Mexico, Canada, Japan, and South Korea—of helping China evade tariffs through transshipment, while President Trump announced tariffs up to 100% on imported drones citing national security [BBC, The Hindu, Le Monde]. In the Middle East, reports emerged of deteriorating conditions aboard the USS Lincoln after a record 260-day deployment supporting operations against Iran, with the USS George Washington now en route as a replacement [France 24, The Hindu]. On the African health front, the DRC's Ebola outbreak spread to a sixth province and is on pace to become the deadliest in history, having already claimed over 2,100 lives [The Guardian]. Japan meanwhile grappled with unprecedented rainfall in Chiba prefecture that killed at least six people and stranded thousands during the Bon holiday period [BBC, Al Jazeera].

top_stories.headline: Romania Shuts Down Only Nuclear Plant as Danube Hits Record Lows, Threatening Energy Supply
bullets: Romania began full shutdown of Cernavodă nuclear plant on August 13 after Danube water levels fell to 30-year lows, eliminating 20% of national electricity production
The plant's second 706MW reactor was disconnected from the grid following July shutdown of first reactor; restart not expected within 10 days
Authorities attempted emergency measures including sinking rock-filled barges into the river at a cost of over €2 million to divert water flow
Romania has called for 'responsible consumption' and will rely on wind, solar, coal, gas, and electricity imports to cover the shortfall

top_stories.headline: US Accuses Over 40 Countries of Helping China Evade Tariffs Through 'Shadow Transshipment Network'
bullets: White House report named India, Canada, Mexico, Japan, South Korea, and the EU among countries allegedly facilitating Chinese tariff evasion
Trade adviser Peter Navarro claimed transshipments cost American jobs and billions in revenue, estimating $30-300 billion in goods rerouted
Administration announced plans to deploy AI to detect and penalize transshipment practices
Chinese embassy rejected accusations, stating 'trade wars have no winners' and that agreements on transshipped goods should not harm third parties

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Balanced presentation noting upcoming Trump-Xi meeting and seeking comment from named countries

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Emphasized India's inclusion and detailed specific Indian regions allegedly involved in transshipment

top_stories.headline: Trump Announces Tariffs Up to 100% on Imported Drones Citing National Security
bullets: President Trump imposed 100% tariffs on drones over 25kg with 'national security capabilities' such as thermal cameras, and 25% on smaller drones
Decision targets an industry dominated by Chinese manufacturers and aims to encourage domestic production
Tariffs set to take effect September 3, 2026
FCC had previously warned of risks including unauthorized surveillance, data exfiltration, and direct UAS attacks

sources.framing_note: Article available but content not fully accessible

top_stories.headline: DRC Ebola Outbreak Spreads to Sixth Province, On Track to Become Deadliest in History
bullets: Ebola has now spread to Bas-Uele province after a man traveled from Isiro and died in Buta, bringing affected provinces to six
Current outbreak has killed over 2,100 people from more than 4,500 cases, reaching this toll nearly three times faster than the 2014-16 outbreak
WHO Director General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus stated the outbreak will surpass the deadliest in history (11,000+ deaths) at current pace
No approved vaccines or treatments exist for the rare Bundibugyo strain responsible for this outbreak; Uganda has reported 20 cases in Kampala

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Comprehensive coverage including Africa CDC statements and comparison to 2014-16 outbreak trajectory

top_stories.headline: US Sailors Report Mental Health Crisis on USS Lincoln After Record 260-Day Deployment
bullets: USS Abraham Lincoln has spent a record 260+ uninterrupted days at sea supporting US operations against Iran
Reports indicate declining mental health among crew, supply issues, and some sailors attempting to throw themselves into the sea
USS George Washington has departed from Da Nang, Vietnam and is transiting through the Strait of Malacca as replacement
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth claimed conditions were 'completely misrepresented' while Democratic lawmakers press for Pentagon accountability

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Led with sailor welfare angle and dire conditions framing

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Provided additional context on ship movements and political pushback from Hegseth
